notes:
Two findings that were wrong about the page they described, both found by auditing a large publisher and checking every high and medium by hand.

**A Facebook Like button was reported as a broken tracking pixel.** `connect.facebook.net` serves two different products: the Meta Pixel is `fbevents.js` plus `fbq(…)`, while `sdk.js` is the JavaScript SDK that a Like button, a share widget or an embedded comment thread loads. Docket matched the shared hostname, so any page carrying a social plugin was recorded as having the pixel — then, finding no account id, reported at HIGH that "the Meta Pixel is on the page but cannot fire" and sent the owner to look for an unfilled placeholder in a product they were not using. It now matches the pixel's own library. A pixel that really is staged, and a pixel installed through a tag manager, are both still detected.

**Complete Organization markup was reported as incomplete.** In JSON-LD, two nodes that share an `@id` are one node, and the common pattern is to define a company once and point at it from everywhere else — `"publisher": {"@type": "Organization", "@id": "…#organization"}`. Docket read each of those pointers as its own Organization and said the name was missing, on sites whose name, url and logo were written correctly a few lines away. The tell was that writing the same reference without its `@type` — equally valid — produced no finding at all, so the shape of the reference was deciding the verdict rather than the state of the markup. Nodes are now merged by `@id` before anything is called missing. Where nothing on the page defines the target the finding still fires, which is the genuine defect it was built for.
